title: Romans Establish Pannonia
description: Rome conquered the region west of the Danube, organizing it as the province of Pannonia, which included much of present-day western Hungary.

title: Magyar Conquest of the Carpathian Basin
description: Led by Árpád, the Magyar tribes settled the Carpathian Basin, an event traditionally remembered as the Hungarian homeland-taking (honfoglalás).

title: Coronation of Saint Stephen I
description: Stephen I was crowned the first Christian king of Hungary, founding the kingdom and establishing the Catholic Church across the realm.

title: Battle of Mohács
description: The Ottoman Empire crushed the Hungarian army and killed King Louis II, leading to the partition of Hungary and over a century of Ottoman rule.

title: Austro-Hungarian Compromise
description: The Ausgleich created the dual monarchy of Austria-Hungary, granting Hungary self-government within the Habsburg empire.

title: Treaty of Trianon
description: Following World War I, Hungary lost about two-thirds of its territory and population, reshaping the modern Hungarian state.

title: Hungarian Revolution
description: A nationwide uprising against Soviet-imposed communist rule was crushed by Soviet forces, becoming a symbol of resistance to oppression.

title: Hungary Joins the European Union
description: Hungary became a member of the European Union, integrating with Western European political and economic institutions.

title: Norse Settlement of Iceland
description: Ingólfr Arnarson is traditionally credited as the first permanent Norse settler, founding what became Reykjavík.

title: Founding of the Althing
description: Icelanders established the Althing at Þingvellir, one of the world's oldest surviving parliamentary institutions.

title: Adoption of Christianity
description: The Althing peacefully agreed that Iceland would convert to Christianity, avoiding civil conflict between pagans and Christians.

title: Old Covenant with Norway
description: Iceland accepted the rule of the Norwegian crown through the Gamli sáttmáli, ending the Commonwealth period.

title: Republic of Iceland Founded
description: Iceland formally declared independence from Denmark and established a republic during World War II.

title: Vigdís Finnbogadóttir Elected President
description: Vigdís became the world's first democratically directly elected female head of state.

title: Icelandic Financial Crisis
description: The collapse of Iceland's major banks triggered a severe economic crisis and sweeping reforms.

title: Construction of Newgrange
description: The Neolithic passage tomb at Newgrange was built, predating the Egyptian pyramids and aligned with the winter solstice.

title: Mission of Saint Patrick
description: Saint Patrick is traditionally said to have begun his Christian mission in Ireland, spreading Christianity across the island.

title: Norman Invasion of Ireland
description: Anglo-Norman forces landed in Ireland, beginning centuries of English involvement and rule on the island.

title: Great Famine Begins
description: Potato blight caused a catastrophic famine that killed roughly a million people and drove mass emigration.

title: Easter Rising
description: Irish republicans staged an armed rebellion against British rule in Dublin, a pivotal moment toward independence.

title: Irish Free State Established
description: The Anglo-Irish Treaty created the Irish Free State, granting most of Ireland self-government as a dominion.

title: Ireland Joins the EEC
description: Ireland became a member of the European Economic Community, transforming its economy and society.

title: Good Friday Agreement
description: A landmark peace accord largely ended the Troubles in Northern Ireland and established power-sharing institutions.

title: Traditional Founding of Rome
description: Tradition dates the founding of the city of Rome to this year, attributed to Romulus, beginning Roman history.

title: Roman Empire Established
description: Augustus became the first Roman emperor, transforming the Republic into the Roman Empire that dominated the Mediterranean.

title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: The deposition of Romulus Augustulus by Odoacer is commonly marked as the end of the Western Roman Empire.

title: Flourishing of the Renaissance
description: Italian city-states like Florence became cradles of the Renaissance, producing figures such as Dante, Leonardo, and Michelangelo.

title: Unification of Italy
description: The Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed under Victor Emmanuel II, uniting most of the peninsula into a single state.

title: Mussolini's March on Rome
description: Benito Mussolini seized power, establishing a Fascist dictatorship that lasted until World War II.

title: Italy Becomes a Republic
description: Italians voted in a referendum to abolish the monarchy and establish the Italian Republic.

title: Treaty of Rome Signed
description: Italy was a founding signatory of the Treaty of Rome, which created the European Economic Community.

title: Battle of Kosovo
description: Serbian and Ottoman forces clashed at the Field of Blackbirds, a battle that became central to regional historical memory.

title: Ottoman Rule Established
description: Kosovo was incorporated into the Ottoman Empire, beginning centuries of Ottoman administration and Islamic influence.

title: End of Ottoman Rule
description: The Balkan Wars ended Ottoman control of Kosovo, which was incorporated into Serbia and later Yugoslavia.

title: Autonomy Revoked
description: Serbian authorities under Slobodan Milošević stripped Kosovo of its autonomy, escalating ethnic tensions.

title: Kosovo War and NATO Intervention
description: NATO's air campaign ended the conflict, and Kosovo was placed under United Nations administration.

title: Declaration of Independence
description: Kosovo declared independence from Serbia, becoming the youngest country in Europe to do so.

title: Stabilisation Agreement with EU
description: A Stabilisation and Association Agreement with the European Union entered into force, deepening ties with Europe.

title: Founding of Riga
description: Bishop Albert founded Riga, which became a key Baltic trading city and later joined the Hanseatic League.

title: Riga Joins the Hanseatic League
description: Riga became a member of the Hanseatic League, growing into a major commercial hub on the Baltic Sea.

title: Incorporation into Russian Empire
description: After the Great Northern War, Livonia including Riga passed to the Russian Empire under the Treaty of Nystad.

title: Latvia Declares Independence
description: Latvia proclaimed its independence, establishing a sovereign republic after the collapse of empires in World War I.

title: Soviet Occupation
description: The Soviet Union occupied and annexed Latvia, beginning decades of foreign rule interrupted by Nazi occupation.

title: Restoration of Independence
description: Latvia restored its independence amid the dissolution of the Soviet Union.

title: Latvia Joins EU and NATO
description: Latvia became a member of both the European Union and NATO, anchoring itself in Western institutions.

title: Principality of Liechtenstein Created
description: Emperor Charles VI united the lordships of Schellenberg and Vaduz into the Principality of Liechtenstein.

title: Sovereignty under Napoleon
description: Liechtenstein gained sovereignty as a member of the Napoleonic Confederation of the Rhine.

title: Full Independence
description: With the dissolution of the German Confederation, Liechtenstein became fully independent and later disbanded its army.

title: Customs Union with Switzerland
description: Liechtenstein formed a customs and monetary union with Switzerland, adopting the Swiss franc.

title: Women Gain the Vote
description: Liechtenstein granted women the right to vote in national elections following a referendum.

title: Joins the United Nations
description: Liechtenstein became a member of the United Nations, expanding its international engagement.

title: Coronation of King Mindaugas
description: Mindaugas was crowned the first and only King of Lithuania, uniting the Lithuanian lands into a Christian kingdom.

title: Battle of Grunwald
description: Polish-Lithuanian forces decisively defeated the Teutonic Knights, one of medieval Europe's largest battles.

title: Union of Lublin
description: Lithuania and Poland formed the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, a major European power for over two centuries.

title: Annexation by Russian Empire
description: The third partition of the Commonwealth brought most of Lithuania under Russian imperial rule.

title: Restoration of Independence
description: Lithuania declared the re-establishment of its independent state with the Act of February 16.

title: First to Break from USSR
description: Lithuania became the first Soviet republic to declare the restoration of its independence from the Soviet Union.

title: Joins EU and NATO
description: Lithuania joined the European Union and NATO, completing its integration with the West.

title: Founding of Luxembourg
description: Count Siegfried acquired the rock of Lucilinburhuc, around which the city and county of Luxembourg grew.

title: Elevated to a Duchy
description: Luxembourg was raised to the status of a duchy under Emperor Charles IV of the House of Luxembourg.

title: Grand Duchy Created
description: The Congress of Vienna established Luxembourg as a Grand Duchy in personal union with the Netherlands.

title: Treaty of London Guarantees Neutrality
description: The Treaty of London affirmed Luxembourg's independence and neutrality, ordering the dismantling of its fortress.

title: Own Ruling Dynasty
description: Luxembourg gained its own ruling house when the crown passed to the House of Nassau-Weilburg, ending union with the Netherlands.

title: Founding Member of European Community
description: Luxembourg helped found the European Coal and Steel Community, becoming a core builder of the European Union.

title: Schengen Agreement Namesake
description: The Schengen Agreement, signed in Luxembourg's village of Schengen in 1985, came into force abolishing internal border checks.

title: Megalithic Temples Built
description: Malta's prehistoric temples such as Ġgantija were constructed, among the oldest free-standing structures in the world.

title: Shipwreck of Saint Paul
description: According to tradition, the Apostle Paul was shipwrecked on Malta, introducing Christianity to the islands.

title: Knights of St John Arrive
description: The Knights Hospitaller were granted Malta by Emperor Charles V, ruling and fortifying the islands for centuries.

title: Great Siege of Malta
description: The Knights and Maltese repelled a massive Ottoman invasion, a celebrated victory in Mediterranean history.

title: British Take Control
description: Malta came under British control after Maltese rebels and British forces expelled Napoleon's garrison.

title: George Cross Awarded
description: Malta was awarded the George Cross for its endurance under heavy Axis bombardment in World War II.

title: Malta Gains Independence
description: Malta became an independent state within the Commonwealth, later becoming a republic in 1974.

title: Malta Joins the European Union
description: Malta became a member of the European Union, the smallest member state by population at the time.

title: Founding of the Principality of Moldavia
description: The medieval Principality of Moldavia emerged under Bogdan I, becoming a significant power in the region.

title: Reign of Stephen the Great Begins
description: Stephen the Great ruled Moldavia, defending it against the Ottomans and founding numerous churches and monasteries.

title: Bessarabia Ceded to Russia
description: The Treaty of Bucharest transferred the eastern part of Moldavia, Bessarabia, to the Russian Empire.

title: Union with Romania
description: Bessarabia proclaimed union with Romania following the collapse of the Russian Empire.

title: Soviet Annexation
description: The Soviet Union annexed Bessarabia and created the Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic.

title: Independence from Soviet Union
description: Moldova declared independence amid the dissolution of the Soviet Union.

title: EU Association Agreement
description: Moldova signed an Association Agreement with the European Union, deepening political and economic ties with Europe.

title: Genoese Fortress Founded
description: Genoa began building a fortress on the Rock of Monaco, marking the origin of the modern settlement.

title: Grimaldi Seizes Monaco
description: François Grimaldi captured the fortress of Monaco, beginning the Grimaldi dynasty's enduring rule.

title: Title of Prince Adopted
description: Honoré II took the title of Prince of Monaco, formalizing the principality's status.

title: Independence Recognized
description: A treaty with France recognized Monaco's sovereignty while it ceded Menton and Roquebrune.

title: Monte Carlo Casino Opens
description: The famous casino opened, helping transform Monaco into a renowned destination for tourism and gaming.

title: First Monaco Grand Prix
description: The inaugural Monaco Grand Prix was held, becoming one of the most prestigious motor races in the world.

title: Monaco Joins the United Nations
description: Monaco became a full member of the United Nations, affirming its place in the international community.

title: Battle of Bar and Duklja's Rise
description: The Slavic state of Duklja, a forerunner of Montenegro, secured autonomy after defeating Byzantine forces.

title: Ottoman Pressure on Zeta
description: The Crnojević rulers of Zeta lost their lowland holdings to the Ottomans, with resistance continuing in the mountains.

title: Prince-Bishopric Established
description: Montenegro became a theocratic prince-bishopric (vladika), blending religious and political leadership.

title: Independence Recognized
description: The Congress of Berlin formally recognized Montenegro's independence after centuries of resistance to Ottoman rule.

title: Kingdom of Montenegro Proclaimed
description: Prince Nicholas I declared Montenegro a kingdom, elevating his title to king.

title: Union with Yugoslavia
description: Montenegro joined the newly formed Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, later Yugoslavia.

title: Restoration of Independence
description: Montenegrins voted in a referendum to restore independence, peacefully separating from Serbia.

title: Montenegro Joins NATO
description: Montenegro became a member of NATO, marking a major step in its Euro-Atlantic integration.

title: Roman Conquest of the Low Countries
description: Julius Caesar's campaigns brought the southern Low Countries under Roman control during the Gallic Wars.

title: Act of Abjuration
description: The northern provinces renounced allegiance to Spain's King Philip II, a foundational step toward Dutch independence.

title: Dutch East India Company Founded
description: The VOC was established, becoming the world's first publicly traded company and a global trading power.

title: Peace of Westphalia
description: Spain formally recognized Dutch independence, ending the Eighty Years' War and confirming the Dutch Republic.

title: Dutch Golden Age
description: The 17th century saw extraordinary Dutch achievements in trade, science, and art, including Rembrandt and Vermeer.

title: Kingdom of the Netherlands Founded
description: Following Napoleon's defeat, the Congress of Vienna established the Kingdom of the Netherlands under the House of Orange.

title: Hunger Winter
description: A severe famine struck the Nazi-occupied western Netherlands during the final winter of World War II.

title: First Country to Legalize Same-Sex Marriage
description: The Netherlands became the first nation in the world to legalize same-sex marriage.

title: Rise of the Ancient Macedonian Kingdom
description: The ancient kingdom of Macedon emerged in the region, later becoming a major power under Philip II and Alexander the Great.

title: Roman Province of Macedonia
description: Rome organized Macedonia as a province after defeating the Macedonian kingdom, integrating it into the empire.

title: Ohrid Literary School
description: Saints Clement and Naum established a major center of Slavic literacy and learning at Ohrid, spreading Christianity and writing.

title: Ilinden Uprising
description: Revolutionaries rose against Ottoman rule and briefly proclaimed the Kruševo Republic, a key event in national memory.

title: Founding of Macedonian Republic in Yugoslavia
description: A Macedonian republic was established within socialist Yugoslavia, recognizing a distinct Macedonian nationhood.

title: Independence from Yugoslavia
description: Macedonia peacefully declared independence following a referendum as Yugoslavia dissolved.

title: Renamed North Macedonia
description: Under the Prespa Agreement with Greece, the country was renamed North Macedonia, resolving a long-running dispute.

title: North Macedonia Joins NATO
description: North Macedonia became a member of NATO after settling its name dispute with Greece.
